groups.label: Dialectical Education Stages
groups.summary: Socrates establishes a rigorous, age-graded curriculum of service and training to avoid the dangers of premature dialectic, which otherwise breeds lawlessness and moral skepticism in the young.
groups.rationale: Both passages from Book VII address the structured timing, risks, and institutional stages of dialectical philosophical education.

groups.label: Decline to Timocracy & Oligarchy
groups.summary: Traced from the breakdown of the ideal city due to miscalculated breeding, Socrates details the spirited timocratic character and the subsequent fall into oligarchy, marked by property qualifications, economic division, unproductive drones, and avaricious souls.
groups.rationale: Covers the first two phases of political degeneration in Book VIII, charting the transition from the ideal city through timocracy to oligarchical governance and character.

groups.label: Genesis and Nature of Democracy
groups.summary: Arising from impoverished revolt against wealthy oligarchs, democracy institutes liberty, equal power by lot, and diverse constitutions, while fostering unstable individuals governed by unnecessary desires across three distinct civic classes.
groups.rationale: Encompasses the entire discussion in Book VIII of the emergence, societal structure, and personal psychology of democracy.

groups.label: Rise and Misery of Tyranny
groups.summary: Socrates describes how a popular champion transforms into a bloodstained public tyrant through bodyguards and civic purges, corresponding internally to an individual soul enslaved by unlawful master passions and living in perpetual fear.
groups.rationale: Links the transition from demagogic democracy into political tyranny (Book VIII) with the psychological and practical misery of the tyrannical man (Book IX).

groups.label: Philosophic Life and Judgement
groups.summary: Socrates argues for the supremacy of intellectual pleasure based on the philosopher's unique wisdom, concluding with the Myth of Er that details cosmic justice, tenfold retributions, and eternal punishment for tyrannical rulers.
groups.rationale: Both passages address the ultimate validation of justice over injustice, comparing philosophical happiness and pleasure with the cosmic, posthumous reckoning awaiting tyrants.
